newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian Hansapank open to partner offers.
newsitem.headline: Estonian Hansapank open to partner offers.

text.p: The leading bank in the Baltic states, Estonia's Hansapank, reiterated on Tuesday that it was interested in seeking a foreign partner but was waiting for proposals rather than actively looking.
Hansapank already has a 12 percent market share of the Baltic banking market.
"If someone is interested in making proposals, then we will listen to them," deputy chairman Rain Lohmus told Reuters.
He stressed that the bank itself was not seeking partners.
Lohmus refused to comment on whether there had been any interest on becoming a strategic partner from other banks.
Hansapank on Monday said in a bourse statement that it was looking for foreign partners to ensure its development strategy as it attempts to move into the Lithuanian market.
Hansapank has said for a long time that it was planning a move into Lithuania. Other Estonian banks have also said that a move into the southernmost Baltic states was possible.
Last June, Hansapank bought Latvia's Deutsche-Lettische Bank, which became its Latvian subsidary Hansabank-Latvija.
